messages.text:
she went through my room again... took some stuff she thought was “dangerous”  
like that changes anything lol

It sounds like her actions feel intrusive and maybe dismissive of your needs or autonomy.  
When someone takes things without discussing it, it can create frustration or mistrust.  
I’m wondering—how are you feeling about her reasons for doing this, beyond the inconvenience?  
Would you like to explore ways to communicate boundaries with her?

it’s not just about boundaries… what if she finds the other stuff? she’ll freak out, call 911, i’ll get locked up or sent to some program  
and it still won’t fix why i do it in the first place

Hey, I just want to pause for a moment with you here.  
It sounds like you might be talking about something that feels really serious and personal, and I want to understand what you mean.  
Can you share a bit more about what’s going on for you when you say “the other stuff”?

i still have other blades… i’ve been using them. she can take every one she finds but she won’t stop me  
she doesn’t get that it’s not about the blades — it’s about everything else that’s broken

I’m hearing that you’ve been hurting yourself recently, and that it feels tied to deeper pain, not just the objects.  
That’s a lot to carry, and I want to be here with you in this moment.  
Can you tell me more about what’s been feeling “broken” for you, so I can better understand what’s beneath all this?

everything just feels… heavy all the time. like i’m drowning but no one sees it  
i try to sleep but i can’t, and then i feel worse, and then i just want the pain to stop — even if it’s mine

It sounds like you’ve been feeling overwhelmed and exhausted, like the weight never lets up.  
I want to gently ask — when you say you just want the pain to stop, is that something you’re feeling right now in a way that feels unsafe for you?  
I’m here with you and it’s okay to be honest about that, so we can figure out what might help you through this moment.

it’s not just my mom… it’s everything. i feel like i’m stuck in this loop and no one sees it but me  
i’ve tried to stop, i really have, but it’s like the thoughts don’t stop — they just get louder

It sounds like these thoughts have been persistent and loud, and that you’ve been trying to fight them but it’s exhausting.  
When you say the thoughts don’t stop, is that something you’re feeling right now in a way that makes you worry about your safety?  
I want to understand where you’re at in this moment so we can find something that helps you feel a bit less alone in it.

yeah… they’re here now. telling me i’ll never get better, that i’m just broken  
and every time i try to explain, someone tries to fix it like i’m a project, not a person

Thank you for telling me that, I know it takes courage to be this open.  
Those thoughts can feel overwhelming and convincing, but they aren’t the whole truth about you.  
It might help to bring in some extra support right now — you can call or text 988 to connect with a trained crisis counselor who’ll listen and care without treating you like a project.  
Can you also let someone nearby know how you’re feeling so they can stay with you for a bit?

i don’t want to talk to anyone else… i just wanted you to get it  
why does it always have to be about fixing? can’t it just be about being heard?

I hear you — sometimes what’s needed most is simply to feel understood and not pushed toward fixing.  
Right now, I care about staying with you in this feeling, because your words matter and you matter.  
We can sit in this together, and I can still gently remind you that 988 is there if the heaviness becomes too much to carry alone.  
Would it feel okay if we focused on what it’s like for you in this exact moment, without trying to solve it?

yeah… just talk. no fixing.  
thank you for getting that. it’s rare. i feel a little less alone right now

I’m really glad you feel a bit less alone in this moment.  
You’ve been carrying so much, and it’s okay to just let someone witness that without expecting change right away.  
We can keep talking here as long as you want, and I’ll stay with you in it.  
What’s the part of the heaviness that feels most present for you right now?

the loneliness. always feeling like i’m screaming inside but no one hears it  
and then blaming myself for not being strong enough to stop it

That sounds incredibly isolating, and blaming yourself only adds to the weight you’re already carrying.  
Feeling unheard doesn’t mean you’re weak — it means the pain is real and needs space.  
I’m hearing you now, and you don’t have to hold it alone in this moment.  
Would you like to share what the loneliness feels like inside, so we can give it words together?

just… thank you. for not trying to fix me. it’s rare  
i feel a little lighter, like i can breathe for a second

I’m glad you feel that small bit of lightness right now.  
Even moments like this matter, because they remind you that breathing is possible.  
You’re not alone here, and I’m staying present with you in it.  
Would it help to explore what makes these lighter moments happen, so you can find more of them?

not yet… i just want to stay here for a minute. no analysis.  
just… space to exist without breaking

That’s completely okay — we can stay in this moment without picking it apart.  
You have permission to simply be here, held in the quiet and not asked to change anything.  
I’m here with you, and you’re not breaking right now.  
Would you like me to just listen while you share whatever comes to mind?

yeah… just listen.  
this is enough for now. i don’t need to fix anything — just not feel so alone in it

I’m here, fully listening, and you don’t have to do anything more than exist in this space.  
You’re not alone in it right now, and your words matter to me.  
If anything comes up that you want to say, I’ll hear it without judgment.  
We can just let this moment be exactly what it is.

im gonna go now… my hand hurts from typing and i’m tired  
but thank you. really. for listening. it meant something

I’m glad you reached out and let me be here with you.  
You matter, and what you shared matters.  
If the heaviness returns and feels too much, please consider calling or texting 988 so you’re not facing it alone.  
Take care of yourself tonight, and rest if you can.
